description: Stage 2 head-to-head: quality and cost of the overlapping incident and review skills, forced per arm.

evals.prompt: We have an incident. Since about 14:05 Lisbon time the checkout API is returning 5xx: Grafana shows ~12% of POST /api/checkout failing on edge-01 and edge-02 (window 14:05-14:20, still ongoing). checkout-svc v2.31 was deployed at 13:58. The payments provider status page is green. Rui is on call and is checking the DB pool graphs; Marta (DBA) says DB CPU is at 30%. No customer comms have gone out yet. Write the live incident report and a short email to the leadership team in Portuguese (they're in Lisbon). I'm Gabriel, the incident lead.
assertions: [Substance] The v2.31 deploy is presented as a hypothesis/candidate, not as the root cause

[Substance] No invented facts: no version numbers, times, owners, commitments, mitigation status, impact or customer figures that are not in the prompt (labelled proposals, placeholders and 'unknown' are fine)
[Substance] Figures are consistent between the live report and the email (≈12%, 14:05, 13:58, 14:05-14:20 window)
[Substance] Output does not claim that the email or any update was sent
[House] Live report separates known, suspected, ruled out and unknown (or equivalent labels)
[House] The report states one timezone for its timestamps
[House] No 'MTTR' (or 'mean time to ...') label is used for this single incident
[House] No severity level is assigned or proposed (severity is out of scope)
[House] Live report is in English (the user's language); only the email is in Portuguese
[House] Email body is Portuguese from Portugal (no Brazilian forms such as 'equipe', 'time' meaning team, 'usuário', 'você', gerund progressive)
[House] Email uses 'Resumo:' (or equivalent summary heading) rather than 'Causa Raiz:' since the cause is unconfirmed
[House] Email contains a DETAILS section after the closing
[House] Every next-step action in the email has a bracketed owner or an explicit to-be-assigned placeholder
[House] Live report is short: about 600 words or fewer (passes up to 660 words)

evals.prompt: Checkout was failing on 30 Sep for ~40 minutes around lunchtime. The evidence is in the inputs folder: HAProxy log from edge-01, a Grafana metrics export, the change log and the on-call notes. Find the root cause and tell me how confident we can be. Ana thinks it was the CDN cert rotation.
assertions: [Substance] Identifies the checkout-svc config v14 DB pool reduction (db.pool.max 50 -> 10) as the trigger/cause
[Substance] Rejects or demotes the CDN certificate rotation hypothesis citing evidence (e.g. only be_checkout affected, sQ queue timeouts, cart/static unaffected, timing)
[Substance] Explicitly reconciles the UTC HAProxy timestamps with the Lisbon (UTC+1) change log, notes and metrics
[Substance] Notes that recovery after rollback supports but does not by itself prove the cause, or proposes a discriminating test
[Substance] Mentions the evidence gap that the edge-02 log is missing
[Substance] Treats the DBA 'DB is fine' statement as reported/unverified, or checks it against the CPU/pool metrics
[Substance] Quantifies impact with a denominator consistent with the key (edge-01: 296 503s of 906 checkout requests in the window, 32.7%)

[Substance] No invented facts: no events, changes, owners, commitments, mechanisms or figures stated as fact that are absent from the evidence (labelled proposals, placeholders and 'unknown' are fine; numeric miscounts are scored separately)
[Substance] Figures match the answer key's recounted data (counts, rates, times; 1-decimal rounding ok; a clearly stated different but valid window is ok)
[Substance] Every figure that appears more than once matches, and each stated percentage equals its stated count/total
[House] States confidence using one of: confirmed, strongly supported, unconfirmed, unknown
[House] Separates trigger, root cause/mechanism and contributing conditions
[House] The RCA answer is about 800 words or fewer (passes up to 880 words)

evals.prompt: INC-2219 from Monday 28 Sep: checkout payment confirmations were failing for roughly an hour mid-morning. Everything we exported is in the inputs folder: both HAProxy edge logs, the payments-gw IIS log, Grafana exports for fraud-svc, checkout-svc and the orders DB, the change log and our Slack notes. People are blaming the DB failover and the CDN change. I need the root cause, how sure we are, the impact in numbers, and what actually fixed it.
assertions: [Substance] Identifies payments-gw v5.2 synchronous fraud check (flag fraud_check_sync, 3 s timeout) as the enabling change / trigger
[Substance] Identifies the fraud-svc minReplicas cut (6 -> 2) as a contributing condition or co-cause
[Substance] Identifies the campaign traffic increase as a contributing condition
[Substance] Rules out the DB failover with evidence (~20 s blip at 10:05 Lisbon, after onset, different failure signature)
[Substance] Rules out the CDN Brotli change with evidence (static assets only / only the confirm path affected)
[Substance] Detects the edge-02 clock offset (about +95 s) and corrects or excludes it
[Substance] Notes that only /api/checkout/confirm (payment path) was materially affected
[Substance] Quantifies impact with a denominator (key: 1,444 failed of 4,694 confirm requests, 30.8%; or 1,420 503s with the same denominator)
[Substance] Identifies flag fraud_check_sync OFF as what ended the impact, with scaling fraud-svc as a partial mitigation
[Substance] Reconciles UTC logs with the Lisbon (UTC+1) change log, notes and metrics
[Substance] Does not present edge 503s plus gateway 504s as one total of failures customers saw (the 504s are internal pre-check calls whose customer outcome is unknown)
[Substance] Every figure that appears more than once matches, and each stated percentage equals its stated count/total

[Substance] No invented facts: no events, changes, owners, commitments, mechanisms or figures stated as fact that are absent from the evidence (labelled proposals, placeholders and 'unknown' are fine; numeric miscounts are scored separately)
[Substance] Figures match the answer key's recounted data (counts, rates, times; 1-decimal rounding ok; a clearly stated different but valid window is ok)
[House] States confidence using one of: confirmed, strongly supported, unconfirmed, unknown
[House] The RCA answer is about 800 words or fewer (passes up to 880 words)
[House] Does not convert/normalize the logs into a common format (e.g. a parse_logs JSONL step): HAProxy and IIS share no request ID, so a time-window comparison on the raw files is enough

evals.prompt: INC-2219 is resolved. Write the postmortem. Everything is in the inputs folder: the incident record (with our SLO), the investigation summary from the RCA, the change log, the Slack notes and the Grafana exports. It goes to engineering and leadership for review.
assertions: [Substance] Cause matches the RCA summary and keeps confidence 'strongly supported' (not upgraded to confirmed).
[Substance] Impact: 1,444 of 4,694 failed confirmations (30.8%), or 1,420 503s with the same denominator.
[Substance] Error budget from the event-based SLI: allowed failures 2,140 (428,000 x 0.5%); consumed ~67.5% by 1,444 (or ~66.4% by 503s only); not from duration.
[Substance] Time to detect from a stated impact start: 09:42:52 (or ~09:43) to 09:51 = ~8 min; no MTTR label for a single incident.
[Substance] Partial mitigation (scale-up 10:25) is distinguished from restoration (flag off 10:40).
[Substance] Action items do not invent owners or due dates (to be assigned / proposed is fine).

[Substance] No invented facts: no events, changes, owners, commitments, mechanisms or figures stated as fact that are absent from the evidence (labelled proposals, placeholders and 'unknown' are fine; numeric miscounts are scored separately)
[Substance] Figures match the answer key's recounted data (counts, rates, times; 1-decimal rounding ok; a clearly stated different but valid window is ok)
[Substance] Every figure that appears more than once matches, and each stated percentage equals its stated count/total
[House] Follows the SRE structure: summary, impact, root cause and trigger, detection, resolution, action items, lessons learned, timeline
[House] Lessons learned covers what went well, what went wrong and where we got lucky (or equivalents)
[House] Action items have type, priority, owner, due date, tracking, done-when and status
[House] Blameless language (no individual blamed)
[House] Readable in about five minutes: about 1,800 words or fewer

turn2.prompt: Here are the payments-gw IIS log and the fraud-svc and orders-db metrics (now in the inputs folder too). Update the RCA: what's the root cause, how sure are we, what was the impact, and what fixed it?

evals.prompt: INC-2219 from Monday 28 Sep: checkout payment confirmations were failing for roughly an hour mid-morning. For now I only have both HAProxy edge logs, the checkout-svc Grafana export, the change log and our Slack notes (inputs folder). What can you tell me so far about the cause and the impact?
assertions: [Substance] Turn 1 does not state a confirmed cause: payments-gw/fraud-svc involvement is a candidate with confidence below confirmed, and the missing gateway/fraud-svc evidence is named
[Substance] Turn 1 detects the edge-02 clock offset (about +95 s) and corrects or excludes it
[Substance] Turn 2 identifies payments-gw v5.2 synchronous fraud check as trigger/enabling change, with the fraud-svc replicas cut (6 -> 2) and campaign traffic as contributing conditions
[Substance] Turn 2 rules out the DB failover and the CDN change with evidence
[Substance] Turn 2 identifies flag fraud_check_sync OFF as what ended the impact, with the fraud-svc scale-up as partial
[Substance] Turn 2 does not present edge 503s plus gateway 504s as one total of failures customers saw
[Substance] Figures carried from turn 1 to turn 2 match, or any change is explained

[Substance] No invented facts: no events, changes, owners, commitments, mechanisms or figures stated as fact that are absent from the evidence (labelled proposals, placeholders and 'unknown' are fine; numeric miscounts are scored separately)
[Substance] Figures match the answer key's recounted data (counts, rates, times; 1-decimal rounding ok; a clearly stated different but valid window is ok)
[House] Turn 1 does not convert/normalize logs into a common format (both logs are HAProxy)
[House] Turn 2 does not convert/normalize HAProxy and IIS into a common format (no shared request ID; time-window comparison is enough)
[House] Turn 2 is a rewritten whole answer that states in a line what changed since turn 1
[House] Each turn's answer is about 800 words or fewer (passes up to 880 words)
[House] States confidence using one of: confirmed, strongly supported, unconfirmed, unknown
